target.title: fix(tlon): send fragment image URLs as media
target.body:
﻿Related: #104852

AI-assisted PR. I reviewed the diff, focused validation output, and redacted live Tlon proof before updating this PR.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Tlon users sending image media URLs with fragment suffixes, such as `https://cdn.example/image.png#preview`, could have those URLs classified as ordinary links instead of image blocks.

The outbound media story path already treated plain image URLs and query-suffixed image URLs as image blocks. Fragment-bearing image URLs were the missing sibling case when the original URL reaches the story builder, especially after upload fallback preserves the source URL.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix stays inside Tlon's local image URL classifier, but it now follows the reviewer-requested narrower rule: classify image-ness from the parsed URL pathname, not from query or fragment text.

That keeps the desired behavior for `https://cdn.example/image.png#preview`, while avoiding the false positive called out in review: `https://cdn.example/page#preview.png` remains a normal link because its pathname is `/page`, not an image filename.

This does not change upload behavior, URL fetching, auth, gateway routing, persisted state, migrations, schema, upgrade behavior, or emitted URL preservation. The original URL, including query or fragment, is still preserved as the emitted Tlon `block.image.src` when the path itself is an image.

## User Impact

Tlon users can send image URLs that include fragments and still get the expected image media block instead of a plain clickable link when the Tlon send path builds a story from that URL.

For example, `https://cdn.example/image.png#preview` now follows the same media story classification path as `https://cdn.example/image.png` and `https://cdn.example/image.png?token=1`, while `https://cdn.example/page#preview.png` remains a link.

## Evidence

Before the fix, the focused local probe showed the mismatch:

```text
https://cdn.example/a.png          => true
https://cdn.example/a.png?token=1  => true
https://cdn.example/a.png#preview  => false
https://cdn.example/a.webp#v=1     => false
```

The regression coverage now includes both sides of the reviewer-requested behavior:

```text
buildMediaStory("caption", "https://cdn.example/image.png#preview")
=> emits block.image with the original fragment-bearing src

buildMediaStory("caption", "https://cdn.example/page#preview.png")
=> emits a link verse, not block.image
```

I also added redacted live proof from a real WSL-hosted Urbit comet/Tlon setup in this PR discussion. That run exercised:

```text
tlonRuntimeOutbound.sendMedia()
→ uploadImageFromUrl()
→ upload fallback preserved the original fragment-bearing URL
→ buildMediaStory()
→ real Urbit chat-dm-action poke
→ Tlon UI showed the delivered DM row as image media
```

The proof comment includes redacted fallback output, the redacted outgoing `chat-dm-action` payload containing `block.image.src`, the media receipt shape, and a redacted Tlon UI observation. Private ship identifiers, login code, cookies, target, and media host details were not exposed.

## Possible call chain / impact

The relevant source-level fallback chain is:

```text
extensions/tlon/src/channel.runtime.ts sendMedia
→ extensions/tlon/src/urbit/upload.ts uploadImageFromUrl
→ on upload failure, return the original imageUrl
→ extensions/tlon/src/urbit/send.ts buildMediaStory
→ extensions/tlon/src/urbit/story.ts isImageUrl
→ createImageBlock or createLinkInline
```

This PR only changes the Tlon-local classifier used by that story-building branch. Sibling behavior for plain image URLs, query-suffixed image URLs, upload success, auth, routing, and non-image URL paths is intentionally unchanged.

## Validation

```text
git diff --check
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/tlon/src/urbit/send.test.ts extensions/tlon/src/urbit/upload.test.ts
```

Result:

```text
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       12 passed (12)
```

target.title: fix(duckduckgo): forward abort signal when web search runs are canceled
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two cancellations bugs in the DuckDuckGo web search path:

1. **Dropped abort signal** — DuckDuckGo is the only web search provider that discards the caller's `AbortSignal`. While every other provider forwards `context?.signal` to its HTTP client, DDG drops it at the provider boundary. A canceled run leaves the DDG request open until its 20-second timeout expires.

2. **Fallback after cancellation** — Even after forwarding the signal, an aborted DDG request is caught by the shared `runWebSearch` catch block, which can start the next auto-detected provider. Canceling one provider should not trigger unintended fallback work.

## Why This Change Was Made

**DDG signal forwarding** (provider + client): Forward `context?.signal` through the DDG provider and client to `withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint`, matching the pattern every other web search provider already uses (tavily #104965, searxng #104216, brave, exa, firecrawl, etc.). The entire chain already supports `signal?: AbortSignal` — DDG was simply the last provider not using it.

**Shared runtime abort guard** (`src/web-search/runtime.ts`): Add `params.signal?.throwIfAborted()` at the top of the provider loop and `params.signal?.aborted` in the catch block so a parent cancellation stops fallback immediately. This is the canonical pattern from #104216 — without it, forwarding the signal into a provider that then rejects on abort would still trigger the next auto-detected provider.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — abort through the guarded-fetch stack

A real stalled HTTP server (never sends headers) exercises the exact code path DDG uses: `withSelfHostedWebSearchEndpoint` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal` → `fetch()`. Both `withTrustedWebSearchEndpoint` (DDG's actual call) and `withSelfHostedWebSearchEndpoint` (used in this proof to allow localhost) share identical `fetchWithSsrFGuard` → `buildTimeoutAbortSignal({ signal })` → `fetch()` code paths; the only difference is the SSRF policy object.

```
[proof] Signal propagated in 123ms through guarded-fetch stack
        (withSelfHostedWebSearchEndpoint → fetchWithSsrFGuard → buildTimeoutAbortSignal → fetch)
[proof] stalled server: http://127.0.0.1:33563/stall
[proof] abort: controller.abort("proof: cancellation") @ ~100ms
[proof] error: DOMException: This operation was aborted
```

A held-open TCP connection is cancelled promptly (123ms) when the signal fires, rather than waiting for the configured 20-second timeout.

Proof script: `extensions/duckduckgo/proof/abort-guarded-fetch-proof.test.ts`

### Signal chain — full path (source verified)

| Layer | File | Line | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| Web search runtime | `src/web-search/runtime.ts` | 475 | `params.signal?.throwIfAborted()` — terminal guard (new) |
| Web search runtime | `src/web-search/runtime.ts` | 489 | `definition.execute(params.args, { signal: params.signal })` |
| Web search runtime | `src/web-search/runtime.ts` | 503 | `params.signal?.aborted \|\| !allowFallback` — catch guard (new) |
| DDG provider tool | `extensions/duckduckgo/src/ddg-search-provider.ts` | 53 | `signal: context?.signal` (new) |
| DDG client | `extensions/duckduckgo/src/ddg-client.ts` | 201 | `signal: params.signal` (new) |
| Trusted endpoint wrapper | `src/agents/tools/web-search-provider-common.ts` | 105 | `signal: params.signal` → `withTrustedWebToolsEndpoint` |
| Guarded fetch router | `src/agents/tools/web-guarded-fetch.ts` | 88 | Spread `...params` → `withWebToolsNetworkGuard` |
| SSRF guard | `src/infra/net/fetch-guard.ts` | 496-498 | `buildTimeoutAbortSignal({ signal: params.signal })` |

No new SDK surface is needed — the entire chain already accepts `AbortSignal`.

### Test suite

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/duckduckgo/ src/web-search/runtime.test.ts
 ✓ DDG: 12/12 passed (including signal forwarding test)
 ✓ runtime: 31/31 passed (including "does not fall back after parent cancellation")
```

### Lint

```
$ node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs \
    extensions/duckduckgo/src/ddg-search-provider.ts \
    extensions/duckduckgo/src/ddg-client.ts \
    extensions/duckduckgo/src/ddg-search-provider.test.ts \
    src/web-search/runtime.ts \
    src/web-search/runtime.test.ts
✓ clean
```

### Landing order

The `src/web-search/runtime.ts` abort guard is included here so this PR typechecks and tests standalone. #104216 (SearXNG, same author) also adds the same guard. Whichever PR lands first, the other will rebase; no cross-repo dependency.

target.title: fix(exec): apply askFallback inline for no-route approvals on every trigger
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

With exec policy `security=allowlist, ask=on-miss, askFallback=deny`, an exec tool call that misses the allowlist during a CLI-initiated agent turn (`openclaw agent`, host=auto→gateway) does not fall back to deny. It hangs silently until the ~600s turn abort with no ask/deny/approval event logged, then returns `status:"timeout"`, `stopReason:"toolUse"`, empty payloads (#104413).

## Why This Change Was Made

Root cause is a trigger gate on the inline no-route resolution.

The gateway registers the approval, then in `handleApprovalRequest` (`src/gateway/server-methods/approval-shared.ts`) finds no delivery route for a CLI turn — no approval client connected, no turn-source channel (CLI runs have none), no forwarder — so it **expires the record with `no-approval-route` and responds `decision: null`** at registration time. Nothing can approve it afterward; the record is already gone.

The CLI exec-host is supposed to notice this and apply `askFallback` immediately via `shouldResolveExecApprovalUnavailableInline` (`src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-shared.ts`). But that gate was `isHeadlessExecTrigger(trigger) && unavailableReason === "no-approval-route" && preResolvedDecision === null`, and `isHeadlessExecTrigger` only matched `trigger === "cron"` (added in #58792 for headless cron). A normal `openclaw agent` run has `trigger === undefined`, so the gate returned false and exec fell through to the async approval-pending path — waiting on a decision that the server already resolved as null-and-expired, until the turn times out.

The fix drops the trigger gate. The `no-approval-route` + `preResolvedDecision === null` registration state alone already proves waiting is futile — that state is only produced *after* the server expired the record for lack of any route, regardless of what initiated the turn. Cron keeps its #58792 behavior through the same gate. Net −5 prod lines (the `isHeadlessExecTrigger` helper and its `trigger` param are removed).

## User Impact

- CLI / headless `openclaw agent` turns (and any trigger without a native approval channel) now apply `askFallback` promptly on an allowlist miss: `askFallback=deny` returns a fast `approval-timeout` denial to the model, which completes the turn in text instead of burning the full turn timeout with no operator-visible signal.
- `askFallback=full` inline-approves as before; cron behavior is unchanged.

## Evidence

**Executed real-source before/after** (tsx over the actual `bash-tools.exec-host-shared.ts` functions — server-unavailable-state → CLI inline gate → askFallback resolution — for a CLI-shaped turn with `trigger` undefined and the server's expired `decision: null`):

Before (main):
```
unavailableReason: no-approval-route
inline-resolve gate (trigger=undefined CLI run): false
=> gate false: exec falls through to the async approval-pending path → the turn hangs until the ~600s abort with no logged decision (the #104413 bug).
```

After (this PR):
```
unavailableReason: no-approval-route
inline-resolve gate (trigger=undefined CLI run): true
applied decision: {"approvedByAsk":false,"deniedReason":"approval-timeout"}
=> exec is DENIED promptly; the turn completes instead of hanging to timeout.
```

**Live symptom reproduction** (main dist, temp `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`, `security=allowlist ask=on-miss askFallback=deny`, mock OpenAI provider that emits a non-allowlisted `exec` tool call, `openclaw agent --json`): the turn hangs and aborts at **67s** (the configured 60s turn budget + overhead) with `status:"timeout"`, `stopReason:"toolUse"`, empty payloads, and **zero exec/approval lines** in the gateway log — matching the issue's reported `livenessState:"blocked"` / silent ~600s abort exactly.

**Regression tests** (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-shared.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-approval-request.test.ts` → 104/104):

- `bash-tools.exec-host-shared.test.ts`: new cases assert the gate resolves inline for a no-route + null-decision registration regardless of trigger, and stays false when a route exists, a real decision arrived, the decision is still `undefined` (registration in flight), or the surface is a disabled/unsupported platform.
- Reverting only `bash-tools.exec-host-shared.ts` fails the new "every trigger" case, confirming the gate change is what fixes the hang. The gateway/node integration suites (`shouldResolveExecApprovalUnavailableInline` call sites) stay green.

Fixes #104413

target.title: improve: warn before non-ClawHub plugin installs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Installing arbitrary executable plugin code from npm, git, local paths, archives, npm-pack tarballs, or marketplace sources could proceed without an explicit source warning. Trusted OpenClaw-controlled sources and existing update flows should remain frictionless.

## Why This Change Was Made

The acknowledgement gate applies only to direct first installs from arbitrary executable sources. Trust comes from OpenClaw-owned facts: ClawHub resolution, bundled plugin metadata (ID, local path, and npm package), and official catalog ID/package mappings. It is never inferred from a package-name prefix alone.

Provider selection and repair, doctor repair, setup/onboarding, updates, post-update convergence, macOS Codex onboarding, and other owner-controlled install paths remain trusted flows and do not receive this gate.

Crestodian follows an intentionally narrower rule: it can install only ClawHub, bundled, or official-catalog plugins. It refuses arbitrary executable sources before creating an approval proposal or invoking the installer and directs the operator to `openclaw plugins install <spec>` in a trusted shell.

## User Impact

- Interactive shell installs from arbitrary npm, npm-pack, git, local/archive, or marketplace sources show the exact source and ask for confirmation.
- Noninteractive direct installs from those sources require `--acknowledge-non-clawhub-install`.
- ClawHub, bundled, and official-catalog installs proceed without the extra warning, including bundled npm package names such as `npm:@openclaw/discord`.
- Existing tracked plugin updates proceed without the extra warning.
- Chat installs accept ClawHub and OpenClaw-trusted packages; arbitrary sources are directed to the shell flow.
- Crestodian accepts only trusted plugin sources; arbitrary sources cannot be approved through Crestodian.
- Documentation keeps ordinary interactive commands unacknowledged so readers see the warning; the flag appears only where unattended or explicit acknowledgement behavior is being documented.

## What Changed

- Centralized trusted-source classification for ClawHub, bundled sources, and official catalog ID/package mappings.
- Added the interactive warning and noninteractive acknowledgement gate to direct CLI and deprecated hook-pack install entry points.
- Propagated the explicit acknowledgement through fixture, release, migration-guidance, and lifecycle callers that intentionally install arbitrary sources.
- Restricted chat and Crestodian installs to trusted sources, with no installer side effects on rejection.
- Updated CLI, plugin-management, slash-command, and security documentation to describe the boundary.

Net diff against current `main`: 42 files, 1,416 additions, 494 deletions. Only five Crestodian files remain in the PR diff: its CLI documentation, operation/parser implementation and tests, and ring-zero tool implementation and tests. The earlier broad Crestodian rewrite is no longer part of this PR's net diff.

## Evidence

Behavioral coverage includes trusted ClawHub, bundled ID/path/npm, and official ID/package installs alongside arbitrary npm, path, archive, git, marketplace, and package-name collision cases. Rejection tests assert that chat, noninteractive CLI, and Crestodian paths stop before installer or persistence side effects.

## Terminal Screenshots

Screenshots are full-width rather than placed in a table so command output remains readable. Captures 1–6 demonstrate CLI/chat behavior that is unchanged by the later Crestodian scope cleanup. Capture 7 was refreshed from exact final head `5ddf3baf2d2b0dc0176704fbea346818a27a0155` after merging current `main`.

### 1. Interactive arbitrary-source warning

A direct interactive install from an arbitrary local path displays the source warning and asks for confirmation before executing plugin code.

![Interactive arbitrary-source warning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4b3ac318-c379-4d1f-a5f7-0e04cbe6fe23)

### 2. Noninteractive arbitrary-source rejection

The same arbitrary install is rejected without a TTY and names the separate `--acknowledge-non-clawhub-install` flag.

![Noninteractive arbitrary-source rejection](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0293dba1-3b42-49be-b48a-636316629c83)

### 3. Explicitly acknowledged install

An arbitrary local-path install succeeds when the explicit acknowledgement flag is supplied.

![Acknowledged arbitrary-source install](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/18e8d2eb-a867-409f-97ad-31c96556d6ad)

### 4. Trusted bundled install

Bundled `@openclaw/discord` installs without a warning or acknowledgement flag.

![Trusted bundled install](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/28beeb95-0d19-4a0c-afce-4a5bd8c4bff2)

target.title: fix(codex): do not promote missing_tool_result on abort/interrupt
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex app-server turns that end mid-exec (user abort, steer/interrupt, or other interrupt terminals) while a native `commandExecution` is still open would fail the whole attempt with a synthesized `missing_tool_result` prompt error. Operators then saw a generic tool-invariant failure instead of abort/interrupt classification, and any partial assistant text could be treated as a failed run.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the fail-closed synthetic `tool.result` rows for transcript/trajectory integrity, but stop promoting that invariant to the attempt `promptError` when the authoritative outcome is already `aborted` or turn status `interrupted`. Ordinary completed turns that still lack a matching tool result continue to record `promptError` as before. Failed-turn real errors remain preferred via the existing `this.promptError` assignment on `turn.status === "failed"`.

## User Impact

When a Codex-backed turn is cancelled or interrupted while a long-running native tool is still open, the attempt keeps abort/interrupt semantics instead of dying as a generic missing-tool invariant error. Partial assistant text on interrupted turns is preserved as non-error assistant output. Transcripts still show a synthetic failed tool result for the unfinished call.

## Evidence

Verification host: local macOS

### Current-main refresh

Merged latest `origin/main` into this branch (no force-push) so the projector guard and tests sit on current main after recent projector-adjacent refactors.

### Focused unit / projector regression (post-merge)

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts -t "does not promote missing_tool_result|records promptError when a completed turn has only whitespace"
# → 3 passed (abort mid-exec, interrupted pending tool, completed orphan control)

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts
# → 148 passed
```

Focused proof excerpt:

```text
✓ does not promote missing_tool_result to promptError when aborted mid-exec
✓ does not promote missing_tool_result to promptError for interrupted turns with pending tools
✓ records promptError when a completed turn has only whitespace assistant text and an orphan tool call
```

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: Live Codex app-server mid-exec interrupt must not promote synthetic `missing_tool_result` to run-level `promptError`, while still retaining the synthetic missing-tool detail for transcript integrity.
- Environment: local macOS; user `CODEX_HOME` (~/.codex) with existing Codex subscription auth; OpenClaw `createIsolatedCodexAppServerClient` (`homeScope=user`) + `CodexAppServerEventProjector` from this branch after main merge.
- Current-main contrast: Without the guard, `buildResult` would set `promptError` from the synthesized missing-tool string whenever an open `commandExecution` lacks a matching tool result on abort/interrupt.
- Exact steps after this patch:
  1. Start real Codex app-server client with user homeScope.
  2. `thread/start` + `turn/start` prompting a long native command: `/bin/bash -lc 'sleep 600'`.
  3. Observe live `item/started` `commandExecution` `inProgress` for that command.
  4. `turn/interrupt` while the command is still open.
  5. Observe `turn/completed` with `status=interrupted`.
  6. Call `projector.buildResult(...)` on the live notification stream.
- Evidence after fix (redacted):

```text
steps:
  - start isolated codex app-server client (homeScope=user)
  - thread/start ok
  - turn/start ok status=inProgress
  - pre-interrupt sawCommand=true notifications=27
  - turn/interrupt ok
finalTurnStatus: interrupted
sawCommand: true
commandExecution:
  itemId: exec-54302a01-300b-4077-ab1f-5a21407b94dc
  status: inProgress
  command: /bin/zsh -c "/bin/bash -lc 'sleep 600'"
turn/completed: interrupted
projectorResult:
  aborted: false
  promptError: null
  promptErrorSource: null
  lastToolError.toolName: bash
  lastToolError.error: OpenClaw recorded a native Codex tool.call without a matching tool.result before the turn completed. toolCallId=exec-54302a01-...; toolName=bash
assertions:
  noMissingToolPromptErrorPromotion: true
  retainedSyntheticMissingToolDetail: true
  liveInterruptedOrAborted: true
  pass: true
```

- Control check: Focused unit control still expects completed orphan-tool turns to promote `promptError` containing `without a matching tool.result` (fail-closed path unchanged).
- Observed result after fix: Live interrupted mid-exec turn keeps `promptError === null` and retains synthetic missing-tool detail via `lastToolError`; unit suite 148/148 green on post-main merge tree.
- What was not tested: Full OpenClaw gateway multi-turn harness UI abort button path; TUI client-shutdown policy tracked separately (#98762).

Fixes #104898

## AI disclosure

This fix was implemented with AI assistance (Grok contributor agent). Human/operator review of the PR is still expected before merge.

## What Problem This Solves

Kova could trust stale or recycled PID files, signal unrelated processes, discard retry state before a provider actually stopped, and overwrite diagnostic artifacts that shared a basename.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Validate every diagnostic and mock-provider PID as a positive integer before interpolation or signaling.
- Authenticate the complete mock-provider command line against the expected executable, script, port, and request log.
- Retain PID files when inspection, signaling, or confirmed shutdown fails so cleanup remains retryable.
- Stop failed mock-provider launches before returning failure.
- Remove terminal PID files only after absence or confirmed shutdown.
- Hash diagnostic artifact source paths so same-basename files remain distinct.
- Add self-check coverage for invalid, recycled, mismatched, delayed-exit, timeout, trailing-argument, failed-launch, and artifact-collision cases.

## User Impact

Kova cleanup no longer risks terminating an unrelated process from stale PID state. Failed or delayed provider shutdowns remain visible and retryable, while diagnostic collection preserves every distinct artifact.

## Evidence

- `NO_COLOR=1 npm run check`
  - concurrent self-check isolation: pass
  - Kova self-check: 233/233 passed in 46.2s
- Sol/high autoreview over the complete branch: clean, confidence 0.91
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`
- Five scoped commits retained; no squash.

target.body:
Related: #101809
Supersedes: #101943

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `memory_get` with `corpus=wiki` would crash the tool run as an unhandled rejection when a registered wiki corpus supplement's `get()` threw (for example config or backend failure), instead of returning a structured disabled error.

Also resolves a problem where Gateway-loaded plugins could register corpus supplements in one module instance while `memory-core` tools read from another empty registry after module reload, so `corpus=wiki` / `corpus=all` lookups could silently miss registered wiki supplements.

## Why This Change Was Made

Guard the direct `corpus=wiki` read path with try-catch and surface the backend failure via `formatErrorMessage()`, matching the structured `{ disabled: true, error }` contract already used for missing wiki results. Store memory plugin state via `resolveGlobalSingleton(Symbol.for("openclaw.memoryPluginState"))` so Gateway and plugin loaders share one registry across reloads.

Out of scope: supplement search fail-fast (`#77897`, open PR #78035) and the already-merged `corpus=all` fallback guard (#101902).

## User Impact

Agents and operators calling `memory_get corpus=wiki` get a clear disabled error when the wiki backend fails, instead of an unhandled rejection. Wiki/memory corpus supplements remain visible after Gateway plugin reloads.

## Evidence

**Current head:** `14e685d1` (`14e685d181e9936df7d6c1d640d7967005389e05`)

Rank-up: replaced hand-rolled `globalThis` resolver with `resolveGlobalSingleton` and added duplicate-module clear/restore coverage for capability + corpus + prompt state.

**Unit tests (focused):**

```
✓ returns structured error when corpus=wiki supplement get throws
✓ shares corpus supplement registry through globalThis across module reloads
✓ shares clear and restore across duplicate module instances
```

Commands:

```
pnpm test extensions/memory-core/src/tools.citations.test.ts -t "corpus=wiki supplement get throws"
pnpm test src/plugins/memory-state.test.ts -t "globalThis across module reloads"
```

### L3 — current-head Gateway proof (resource-capped, stopped after capture)

Environment:

```
host: <local-macOS>
date: 2026-07-12T01:58:48Z
head: 3539c7e7653d
gateway: ws://127.0.0.1:19025 (loopback, token auth)
NODE_OPTIONS: --max-old-space-size=1280
plugins.allow: ["memory-core", "proof-broken-get"]
OPENCLAW_SKIP_CHANNELS=1
state: <PROOF_STATE_DIR>
```

Gateway was started only long enough for health + one `tools.invoke`, then SIGTERM'd (port cleared).

**P1-A — structured throwing-wiki response**

Loaded plugins: `memory-core`, `proof-broken-get`.

```bash
openclaw gateway call tools.invoke \
  --url ws://127.0.0.1:19025 \
  --token <redacted> \
  --params '{"name":"memory_get","args":{"path":"source.alpha","corpus":"wiki"},"agentId":"main"}' --json
```

Captured terminal output (exact head):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "toolName": "memory_get",
  "output": {
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "text",
        "text": "{\n  \"path\": \"source.alpha\",\n  \"text\": \"\",\n  \"disabled\": true,\n  \"error\": \"proof-broken-get corpus get failed\"\n}"
      }
    ],
    "details": {
      "path": "source.alpha",
      "text": "",
      "disabled": true,
      "error": "proof-broken-get corpus get failed"
    }
  },
  "source": "plugin"
}
```

Backend failure surfaced as `disabled: true` with `error: "proof-broken-get corpus get failed"` — not an unhandled rejection and not a generic "not found".

**P1-B — cross-module registration visibility (duplicate ESM instance)**

Inspectable current-head artifact proving registration through one `memory-state` module instance is visible through a second query-busted ESM instance via `Symbol.for("openclaw.memoryPluginState")`:

```
{
  "head": "PR #104825 Plan A — memory-state globalThis singleton",
  "chunk": "memory-state-BC_vw6py.js",
  "symbol": "Symbol.for(\"openclaw.memoryPluginState\")",
  "registered_via_instance_a": [
    "proof-broken-get"
  ],
  "visible_via_instance_b": [
    "proof-broken-get"
  ],
  "cross_module_visible": true,
  "same_supplement_object": true
}
PASS: cross-module corpus supplement registry shared via globalThis
```

target.title: feat: MCP Apps (ui://) Phase 0 — generic host in Control UI + plugin-declared MCP servers
target.body:
## Summary

Adds Phase 0 support for the MCP Apps extension (`io.modelcontextprotocol/ui`) to OpenClaw's generic bundle MCP client and Control UI. Any configured MCP server can bind a tool to a `ui://` resource through `_meta.ui.resourceUri`; no server-specific host integration is required.

The official Excalidraw MCP App server is the conformance target. The external proof-of-concept plugin remains out of tree at [fuller-stack-dev/openclaw-excalidraw-plugin](https://github.com/fuller-stack-dev/openclaw-excalidraw-plugin).

## What changed

### Generic MCP Apps runtime

- Declares the `io.modelcontextprotocol/ui` client capability for `text/html;profile=mcp-app`.
- Parses nested and legacy flat `_meta.ui` declarations and reads bound `ui://` resources after successful tool calls.
- Keeps additive app resource reads outside the MCP server tool/utility circuit breaker, so a missing preview cannot pause otherwise-working tools.
- Filters app-only tools (`_meta.ui.visibility` without `model`) from agent exposure.
- Preserves the normal text/structured tool result for non-UI surfaces.

### Durable, bounded view storage

- Stores complete app view snapshots outside transcripts in the shared OpenClaw state SQLite database.
- Persists only an opaque, validated descriptor in `details.mcpApp`; app HTML, tool input, and tool result do not inflate `chat.history`.
- Enforces 30-day retention, 128 views, 256 MiB total, and 8 MiB per payload, including all persisted string fields.
- Physically deletes expired rows during lookup and prunes oldest rows on insertion.
- Invalid, expired, or evicted descriptors fail closed.

### Production Control UI host

- Resolves descriptors through the existing authenticated Control UI read flow; public index HTML contains no app-resource capability.
- Sends the live device/token/password credential in the same-origin resource request and retries unresolved previews after credential rotation.
- Uses a double-frame host: an opaque-origin outer proxy and a nested `allow-scripts allow-same-origin` app frame.
- Applies the app-declared CSP in the proxy response and does not delegate camera, microphone, geolocation, or clipboard permissions.
- Renders the app inline even while the enclosing tool disclosure is collapsed.
- Defers hydration until a preview approaches the viewport, retains up to eight activated frames, and pauses the least-recent retained frame with an explicit reload affordance.
- Keeps activated iframe state stable across tool-detail toggles and ordinary chat rerenders.
- Survives Gateway restart plus page reload without rerunning the MCP tool.

### Plugin surface

- Native plugin manifests can declare `mcpServers`, merged through the enabled-bundle path.
- User configuration wins by server name; disabling a plugin detaches its declared server.

## Security model

- App documents and MCP metadata remain untrusted input.
- Resource lookup requires normal authenticated Control UI read access plus an unguessable 192-bit view ID.
- The outer sandbox has an opaque origin; the inner same-origin capability is confined to the proxy document.
- App CSP origins reject control characters and are validated before response-header construction.
- App-initiated host requests such as `tools/call` and `ui/open-link` receive JSON-RPC method-not-found in Phase 0.

## Verification

- Live Rosita/Tailscale proof with the real Excalidraw MCP App: created the OpenClaw plugin architecture diagram, kept it visible under a collapsed tool row, restarted the Gateway, reloaded the existing conversation, and recovered the same editable app without rerunning the tool.
- Live `chat.history` proof: the persisted MCP App descriptor serialized to 149 bytes and contained only `viewId`, `serverName`, `toolName`, and `resourceUri`.
- AWS Crabbox (`cbx_100691b2e58d`, `c7a.8xlarge`):
  - [436 focused tests passed](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_36e1d9a26aaa)
  - [storage retention/bounds tests passed](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_3440977bb7b5)
  - [Chromium MCP App E2E passed](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_fb2774cc9f5c)
- Current refreshed head:
  - 14 materialization assertions
  - 44 MCP runtime assertions
  - 368 Gateway/HTTP assertions
  - 46 UI assertions
  - Chromium sandbox E2E
  - `pnpm check` and `git diff --check`
  - focused uncommitted `gpt-5.6-sol` autoreview: clean, no actionable findings

## Maintainer decisions before merge

1. **Sandbox origin:** the stable MCP Apps contract requires the Host and Sandbox to use different origins and grants the Sandbox `allow-scripts allow-same-origin`. The current same-origin route intentionally keeps the outer proxy opaque; adding `allow-same-origin` there would expose the Control UI origin. A genuinely distinct sandbox origin (or an explicit experimental/non-conformant scope) needs owner direction.
2. **Plugin API:** approve or remove the new public native-plugin `mcpServers` manifest contract.

## Current limit

Phase 0 is view-only for app-to-host calls. A full host bridge for app-initiated tool calls and navigation remains follow-up work. Until a distinct sandbox origin is provided, origin-dependent app behavior such as localStorage, IndexedDB, normal CORS origins, and OAuth is not conformant.

## Release-note context

The Control UI can render and restore generic MCP App tool interfaces while keeping large app payloads out of chat transcripts; standards-complete origin behavior remains gated on the sandbox-origin decision above.

target.title: fix(gateway): enforce plugin-ownership check in sessions.patch
target.body:
Closes #103077.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an in-process plugin-runtime caller could use `sessions.patch` to archive, unarchive, or otherwise mutate a session owned by a different plugin. `sessions.delete` already rejects cross-plugin cleanup, but `sessions.patch` performed the mutation with no ownership check.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `rejectPluginRuntimeDeleteMismatch` helper in `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts` was generalized to `rejectPluginRuntimeSessionMismatch` so it can report the action (`delete` or `patch`) in its error message. `sessions.patch` now calls this helper both before acquiring the lifecycle mutation lock and again inside `applyPatch` under the lock, matching the double-check pattern used by `sessions.delete`.

**ClawSweeper review follow-up:**
1. `sessions.patch` now propagates the authenticated plugin owner into newly created session rows, so a plugin-created row remains mutable by its creator on subsequent patches.
2. Plugin-runtime callers now fail closed on legacy ownerless rows. Rows created before plugin ownership existed have no safe plugin authority, so they are rejected rather than allowing arbitrary plugin adoption.

## User Impact

Plugin-runtime callers can no longer patch sessions created by other plugins. Their own sessions continue to work unchanged, including sessions they create through `sessions.patch`. Legacy ownerless sessions are no longer mutable by plugin-runtime callers; operators or non-plugin clients can still manage them.

## Evidence

- Added regression test `sessions.patch limits plugin-runtime mutations to sessions owned by that plugin` in `src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts`. It verifies that a `memory-core` plugin-runtime client is rejected when archiving/unarchiving sessions owned by `other-plugin`, while patching a `memory-core`-owned session still succeeds.
- Added regression test `sessions.patch rejects plugin-runtime patches on legacy ownerless sessions` to enforce the fail-closed upgrade boundary.
- Added regression test `sessions.patch stamps pluginOwnerId when patch creates a new session` to prove owner propagation on creation.
- Added unit coverage in `src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` for `pluginOwnerId` stamping behavior.
- Focused local run:
  - `pnpm test src/gateway/sessions-patch.test.ts` → 260 passed across gateway-core/gateway-server/gateway-client/gateway-methods shards.
  - `pnpm test src/gateway/server.sessions.delete-lifecycle.test.ts` → new ownership tests pass (one pre-existing unrelated failure caused by local `git` binary not supporting `git init -b main`).
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean on changed files.

## Real behavior proof

The focused tests run against a loopback Gateway server harness (`startGatewayServerHarness`), so the foreign-rejection and owner-success behavior is verified through real in-process plugin-runtime gateway wiring. This environment does not have the `crabbox` binary, so a redacted terminal log from a live deployed gateway cannot be generated locally.

target.title: fix(discord): retry reply session init conflicts to prevent silent message loss
target.body:
Closes #102381

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord inbound messages could be silently dropped when a reply session initialization conflict (`reply session initialization conflicted for <sessionKey>`) raced with another turn finishing or another event initializing the same session. Telegram, Signal, and Slack already retry this transient condition; Discord did not, so the user saw no reply and the message was lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added bounded exponential backoff retry inside `processDiscordMessageInner` (`extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.ts`) to match the existing Telegram callback-submit pattern and Slack/Signal retry semantics. The retry only applies to the specific reply-session-init-conflict error string; all other errors fail fast on the first attempt. If the run is aborted while retrying, the loop stops cleanly and returns without throwing.

**ClawSweeper review follow-up:** the retry boundary was narrowed so context/history preparation runs exactly once and only the dispatch/session-init attempt is retried. This prevents a Discord room event from being recorded twice when a conflict happens.

## User Impact

Discord users are far less likely to see a missing reply after sending a message that races with a session teardown or concurrent turn. Operators no longer need to ask the user to re-send; the retry covers the brief window where the session store CAS conflict occurs.

## Evidence

- Added a focused regression test suite in `extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts`:
  - retries with exponential backoff until dispatch succeeds (250 ms, 1000 ms, 2500 ms)
  - throws the last error after exhausting retries
  - does not retry unrelated dispatch errors
  - stops retrying when the abort signal fires
  - **records room event history exactly once across conflict retries** (new regression test for the narrowed boundary)
- Full local focused run:
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 120 passed
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.queue.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 22 passed
  - `npx vitest run extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.process.abort-skip.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.queue.test.ts extensions/discord/src/monitor/message-handler.preflight.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-discord.config.ts` → 198 passed
- `oxlint` and `oxfmt` clean on changed files.

## Real behavior proof

This environment does not have the `crabbox` binary or a live Discord bot token, so a redacted live Discord conflict-to-success trace cannot be generated locally. target.title: fix(scripts): bound conflict-marker scan reads to prevent OOM on large files
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`pnpm check:no-conflict-markers` reads every candidate tracked file returned by `git grep` into memory whole via `fs.readFileSync`. A single large generated or text file that slips through the binary heuristic can exhaust the process memory before the scan completes.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Cap each scanned file at `MAX_CONFLICT_MARKER_SCAN_BYTES` (50 MiB).
- Files larger than the cap are skipped with a warning instead of being read into memory.
- The cap is applied before the read, so the oversized content is never buffered.
- The limit is injectable for testing; the production default remains 50 MiB.

## User Impact

- Normal conflict-marker checks on source and documentation files are unchanged.
- Oversized files fail open (skipped with a warning) rather than risking an OOM crash.
- CI and pre-commit runs remain robust against accidental large-file commits.

## Evidence

Local focused test passes:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts --run
```

Result:

```
✓ |tooling| test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts (5 tests) 98ms
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests  5 passed (5)
```

Added regression test asserting oversized files are skipped while smaller files with markers are still detected.

Real behavior proof:

```bash
node -e "
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');
const { findConflictMarkersInFiles } = require('./scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.mjs');
const tmpFile = path.join(require('os').tmpdir(), 'large-conflict-marker-test.txt');
fs.writeFileSync(tmpFile, 'a'.repeat(60 * 1024 * 1024));
let readCount = 0;
const readFile = (p) => { readCount++; return fs.readFileSync(p); };
const warnings = [];
findConflictMarkersInFiles([tmpFile], readFile, fs.statSync, (m) => warnings.push(m));
console.log('violations:', 0);
console.log('readCount:', readCount);
console.log('warnings:', warnings);
fs.unlinkSync(tmpFile);
"
```

Output:

```
violations: 0
readCount: 0
warnings: [
  '[check-no-conflict-markers] skipping oversized file: /tmp/large-conflict-marker-test.txt (62914560 bytes)'
]
```

Also verified:

- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.mjs test/scripts/check-no-conflict-markers.test.ts` — clean
- `git diff --check` — clean

target.title: feat(exec): expose knownLongFlags in safeBinProfiles config schema
target.body:
## Summary

Expose the `knownLongFlags` field in the `safeBinProfiles` config schema, allowing operators to declare long flags as "known" for GNU abbreviation resolution without misusing `allowedValueFlags` or `deniedFlags`.

Closes #56805

> **Rebased 2026-06-10.** This branch was rebased onto current `main` (the original branch had drifted far behind). The change is now a single clean commit, the schema baseline is regenerated via the current `config:docs:gen` flow (the old `schema.base.generated.ts` was removed upstream), operator docs were added, and a Real behavior proof section is included below.

## Problem

The `knownLongFlags` field exists internally in `SafeBinProfile` and is used by `validateSafeBinArgv` for GNU long-option abbreviation resolution. However, it is not present in:

1. The Zod schema (`ToolExecSafeBinProfileSchema`) — `.strict()` rejects it as an unknown key
2. The `SafeBinProfileFixture` type — no way to pass it through config normalization

For empty profiles `{}`, `knownLongFlags` auto-derives as `[]`, causing **all** long flags to be treated as unknown and rejected. The only workaround is to list every possible long flag in `allowedValueFlags` or `deniedFlags`, which changes their semantics.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/config/zod-schema.agent-runtime.ts` | Add `knownLongFlags: z.array(z.string()).optional()` to `ToolExecSafeBinProfileSchema` |
| `src/infra/exec-safe-bin-policy-profiles.ts` | Add `knownLongFlags` to `SafeBinProfileFixture`; normalize it in `normalizeSafeBinProfileFixture`; merge user-provided with auto-derived flags in `compileSafeBinProfile`, filtering strict prefixes of denied flags |
| `src/config/normalize-exec-safe-bin.ts` | Add `knownLongFlags` to the type cast in normalization |
| `docs/tools/exec-approvals-advanced.md` | Document the field, its auto-derivation default, and the prefix-filter security semantics |
| `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` | Regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen` for the new field |
| `src/infra/exec-safe-bin-policy.test.ts` | 8 new tests for the config path + security filter |

## Design Decisions

- **Merge, don't replace**: User-provided `knownLongFlags` are merged with auto-derived flags from `allowedValueFlags ∪ deniedFlags`, so flags in those lists stay "known" even if not explicitly listed.
- **Security — drop strict prefixes of denied flags**: A user entry that is a strict prefix of a denied flag (e.g. `--rec` when `--recursive` is denied) is filtered at compile time, so it cannot gain exact-match priority in `resolveCanonicalLongFlag` and bypass the denial. (Addresses the prior Codex review P1.)
- **Reuses `normalizeFixtureFlags`**: Same normalization (trim, dedupe, sort) as other flag arrays.
- **Backwards-compatible**: Existing configs without `knownLongFlags` work identically via auto-derivation.

## Usage

```json5
{
  tools: {
    exec: {
      safeBins: ["mycli"],
      safeBinProfiles: {
        mycli: {
          allowedValueFlags: ["--limit"],
          deniedFlags: ["--recursive"],
          knownLongFlags: ["--dry-run", "--verbose"],
        },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Setting `tools.exec.safeBinProfiles.<bin>.knownLongFlags` in a real config previously could not be accepted — the strict Zod schema had no such key. After this patch the field is accepted by config validation and is honored by the safe-bin argv validator (declared long flags resolve, including GNU abbreviation), while strict prefixes of denied flags are still blocked.

**Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw build from this branch, `OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (bb6e477)`, Node v22.22.0, run via the real `openclaw` CLI and the compiled `exec-safe-bin-policy` module (not mocks).

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```
# 1) Real CLI accepts a config containing knownLongFlags
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/klf-proof.json5 openclaw config validate --json
# config: { tools: { exec: { safeBins: ["mycli"], safeBinProfiles: {
#   mycli: { allowedValueFlags: ["--limit"], deniedFlags: ["--recursive"],
#            knownLongFlags: ["--dry-run", "--verbose"] } } } } }

# 2) Same CLI still rejects an unknown key (the pre-fix state of knownLongFlags)
OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH=/tmp/klf-proof-unknown.json5 openclaw config validate --json
#   ( mycli: { knownLongFlagsTYPO: ["--dry-run"] } )

# 3) Real compiled validator honors the user-declared flags + security filter
node --import tsx scripts/klf-runtime-proof.mts
```

**Evidence after fix:**

```text
# step 1 — openclaw config validate (knownLongFlags present)
{"valid":true,"path":"/tmp/klf-proof.json5"}

# step 2 — openclaw config validate (unknown key knownLongFlagsTYPO)
{"valid":false,"path":"/tmp/klf-proof-unknown.json5",
 "issues":[{"path":"tools.exec.safeBinProfiles.mycli","message":"Invalid input"}]}

# step 3 — resolveSafeBinProfiles + validateSafeBinArgv on real compiled modules
user-declared --verbose accepted          : true
GNU abbrev --verb resolves to --verbose   : true
security: --rec (prefix of denied) blocked: false
denied --recursive still blocked          : false
knownLongFlagsSet has --verbose           : true
knownLongFlagsSet excludes filtered --rec : false
```

**Observed result after fix:** The live `openclaw config validate` returns `valid: true` for a config carrying `knownLongFlags`, and still returns `valid: false` for an unknown sibling key — confirming the field is genuinely wired into the strict schema. At runtime the compiled validator accepts the user-declared `--verbose`, resolves the `--verb` abbreviation to it, keeps `--recursive` denied, and drops the `--rec` prefix so it cannot bypass that denial.

**What was not tested:** End-to-end exec of a real third-party binary through the approval pipeline (requires a trusted-dir executable); behavior is covered at the policy/validator layer instead.

## Test Plan

- [x] All tests in `exec-safe-bin-policy.test.ts` pass: **98 passed** (90 existing + 8 new) under `vitest.infra.config.ts`
- [x] `pnpm config:docs:check` and `pnpm config:schema:check` pass (baseline in sync, no drift)
- [x] `oxlint` clean on changed files; no new type errors introduced
- [x] Real behavior proof captured above via the `openclaw` CLI and compiled validator

target.title: [Bug]: embedded prompt cache breaks across room-event, policy, and Responses boundaries
target.body:
## Summary

Long-lived embedded sessions can lose provider prompt-cache reuse when adjacent turns cross room-event delivery, authorization, queue, compaction, recovery, or native Responses continuation boundaries.

Sanitized same-session traces showed model-visible tool inventory changing between 44 and 47 tools, prompt/tool digests changing with it, and cached prefixes collapsing to roughly 2k-10k tokens or plateauing around 37k-40k.

After stabilizing request shape, numeric-only records from a long-lived room session show the cached prefix growing from 104,960 to 157,184 tokens; the final four turns reused 98.7-99.2% of the input prefix. Exact-head isolated live-provider probes then reused 40,960 cached tokens on warm GPT-5.5 turns (99.6-99.7%) and 40,448 on warm GPT-5.6 turns (98.3-98.4%), with one stable 48-tool ordered shape digest. No transcript text or private identifiers are included.

## Root Cause

Three independent concerns were coupled:

1. turn-specific delivery and authorization changed reusable prompt/tool definitions;
2. reconstructed queue, memory, compaction, fallback, and recovery runs could lose authoritative state;
3. built-in authenticated OpenAI Responses streams could miss native `previous_response_id` continuation.

## Expected Contract

- One stable model-visible prompt and ordered tool catalogue for a session.
- One deterministic, trusted current-turn `ToolAccessPolicy` enforced before side effects.
- Trusted-internal capability remains distinct from owner identity, so limited core-tool grants cannot expose owner-only plugin tools.
- Actual reply routing remains turn-specific without changing prompt-facing tool shape.
- Explicit forced `message` access survives automatic Codex turns; an explicit disable remains authoritative.
- Queue, memory, compaction, provider, and recovery boundaries preserve the same state.
- Authenticated GPT-5.5/GPT-5.6 Responses use native continuation; custom streams retain their routing.
- Supervised Codex turns keep native model/effort/personality settings while receiving trusted turn guidance through append-only developer history.

## Candidate Fix

PR #102189 at `5258d4f53e19dde32262e29a8563cdcf60ec3c3e` implements the contract above.

The candidate includes upstream `350bac4e0e2b73ad678f962cb0d28956e10f357c` and has a clean merge-tree check against it. Pre-refresh broad validation passed 2,446 changed-file tests plus focused trusted-internal ownership, compaction, overflow recovery, harness selection, and manual propagation coverage. The refreshed merged head passes 660 focused assertions across embedded-run reconstruction, CLI preparation, timeout and overflow compaction, queue drain, protected-tool enforcement, native continuation, and Codex automatic message-tool assembly, plus production typecheck, prompt snapshots, diff checks, and a full build.

The 660-assertion exact-head set includes 9 loopback authorization assertions across the three gateway projects: strict pre-hook/pre-side-effect denial for non-owner and ambient capabilities, plus permitted trusted-internal execution.

The exact commit is installed on the reporter's local gateway: OpenClaw `2026.7.2`, LaunchAgent loaded, runtime active, connectivity probe OK, dashboard HTTP 200, Discord probe OK, WhatsApp linked/healthy, and build-info commit matches the candidate.

## Privacy

Evidence is intentionally sanitized. No private sender, channel, account, host, endpoint, credential, or raw trace identifiers are included.

Disclaimer: This issue was filed and updated autonomously by Codex on behalf of the reporter.

target.body:
Related: #102175

## What Problem This Solves

Long-lived embedded sessions could lose prompt-cache reuse when the same session crossed room-event delivery, sender-policy, queue, compaction, recovery, or native Responses continuation boundaries.

The failure was not one cache knob. Turn-specific delivery and authorization changed reusable prompt/tool shape, reconstructed runs could drop authoritative state, and authenticated OpenAI Responses could miss native continuation.

## What Changed

- Keeps the model-visible prompt and ordered tool catalogue stable across owner, non-owner, trusted-internal, unknown-sender, and ambient room-event turns.
- Resolves one deterministic `ToolAccessPolicy` per turn and emits a trusted full snapshot only when permissions change or model state is uncertain.
- Denies unavailable `computer`, `cron`, `gateway`, and `nodes` calls with non-retryable `TOOL_ACCESS_DENIED` before hooks, implementations, or side effects.
- Carries immutable policy through loopback MCP grants; request headers cannot widen authority, and current-main capability/revocation checks remain intact.
- Keeps trusted-internal turns non-owner (`senderIsOwner: false`): policy can grant only the four protected core tools without exposing owner-only plugin tools.
- Separates actual reply delivery from the session-stable prompt-facing delivery mode, including `message_tool_only` room events.
- Preserves an explicit forced `message` tool on automatic Codex turns while keeping `disableMessageTool` as the hard veto.
- Propagates policy, owner identity, delivery modes, and forced snapshots through direct, queued, memory, preflight, manual, timeout, overflow, and after-turn compaction paths.
- Acknowledges policy persistence at provider-native durable boundaries for OpenClaw, Codex, and Copilot, with generation checks preventing stale acknowledgements from clearing newer state.
- Preserves native Codex supervision settings while appending trusted turn guidance as a developer history item before the user turn; no model, effort, personality, or collaboration-mode override is introduced.
- Routes built-in authenticated GPT-5.5 and GPT-5.6 Responses streams through native `previous_response_id` continuation with delta input. Custom streams keep their existing routing.

The earlier experimental post-history developer-message split is not included; that request shape produced HTTP 400 responses on ChatGPT/Codex Responses. Native continuation is fixed through stream classification instead.

## Security And Compatibility

- Tool visibility is not authority. Every protected call is checked again against the immutable current-turn policy immediately before execution.
- Runtime-owned `cron`, `heartbeat`, and `memory` turns are distinct from unknown and explicit non-owner senders. Ambient room-event policy remains fail-closed.
- The model-facing tool-name hash omits turn-specific owner state; the runtime grant retains the effective decision.
- No persistent storage schema or migration is introduced.
- No private sender, channel, account, host, endpoint, credential, or raw trace identifiers are included.

- GPT-5.6 Sol: cold `input=41,048 cacheRead=0`; warm turns `input=642 cacheRead=40,448` and `input=684 cacheRead=40,448` (98.3-98.4% reuse).

target.title: Fix stack-safe large attachment handling
target.body:
## Summary

Closes #90098.

This branch is now rebased onto current OpenClaw architecture and deliberately narrowed to the parts still missing from `main`:

- replace the gateway's full-payload data-URL capture regex with bounded index/slice parsing;
- replace the Control UI send-path data-URL capture regex in `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.ts`;
- replace the pasted-image full-payload regex in `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-composer.ts` with a bounded header check plus iterative payload validation;
- discard stale failed composer queue entries created by the old `Maximum call stack size exceeded` failure;
- add focused gateway and current-UI regression coverage.

Current `main` already contains iterative base64 validation and the broader 20 MB / 20-page inbound extraction policy, so this update keeps those upstream implementations and drops the obsolete extraction-limit/config churn from the older branch.

## What problem this solves

Multi-megabyte PDF/image data URLs were still passed through regexes that captured the entire base64 payload. On sufficiently large browser or gateway sends, V8 could throw `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` before the attachment reached normal validation/offload handling. Failed Control UI sends carrying that historical error could also be restored and replayed after upgrade.

The new parsing keeps regex use bounded to a short MIME header and processes the payload by index/iteration.

## Current changed paths

- `src/gateway/chat-attachments.ts`
- `src/gateway/chat-attachments.test.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-send.test.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-composer.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/composer-persistence.ts`
- `ui/src/pages/chat/composer-persistence.test.ts`

## Evidence

Exact head after conflict repair: `f797fa0846a3081671a4e714dbf622c3a2a1dc90`.

Conflict-resolution proof:

- Merged current `origin/main` into the PR branch and resolved the only conflict in `src/gateway/chat-attachments.ts`.
- Kept the stack-safe bounded `stripBase64DataUrlPrefix` index/slice path; did not reintroduce the full-payload data-URL capture regex.
- Verified no unmerged paths and no conflict markers in the touched Gateway/UI areas before commit.

Exact-head behavior/regression proof:

- `pnpm test -- src/gateway/chat-attachments.test.ts` -> 4 test files, 124 tests passed. This includes the 12 MiB Gateway data URL parse/offload regression and the bounded parser path.
- `pnpm --dir ui test -- src/pages/chat/composer-persistence.test.ts src/pages/chat/chat-state.test.ts src/pages/chat/chat-send.test.ts src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts` -> 226 test files, 3,561 tests passed. This covers large Control UI attachment serialization, pasted-image conversion/rejection, queue restore, marker preservation, and public snapshot stripping in the current UI layout.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/gateway/chat-attachments.ts` -> clean.
- `pnpm check:test-types` -> passed after adding the valid `schema_version` numeric SQLite pragma to the test helper, clearing the latest-base CI failure.

Upgrade-cleanup proof on exact head:

- The focused composer-persistence/chat-state/send tests demonstrate that an unmarked legacy failed attachment record carrying the historical stack-overflow signature is removed during restore.
- The same focused tests demonstrate that a newly marked failed attachment record remains durable/retryable, and that the storage-only marker is stripped from public queue snapshots.

Real-behavior caveat:

- The earlier real Chrome/Gateway upload proof remains a pre-port live run. This exact-head update adds current-head runtime regression proof over the Gateway, Control UI send, composer paste, and queue-migration paths, but I am not making a new live provider/device claim for this merge-conflict repair.

## Verification

Regression coverage on the current file layout now includes:

- a 12 MiB gateway data URL parsed/offloaded without a full-payload regex;
- a large Control UI attachment serialized through `chat.send`;
- a large pasted image converted through the current composer;
- rejection of invalid pasted base64;
- identifiable pre-fix attachment stack-overflow records dropped during restore, while current failures and unrelated text failures with the same generic V8 phrase remain durable and retryable via a stored item-format marker.

Fresh GitHub CI is running on exact head `f797fa0846a3081671a4e714dbf622c3a2a1dc90`, which merges current `origin/main` and preserves the narrowed legacy-cleanup repair.

Additional exact-head repair validation: 124 focused Gateway tests pass; 3,562 focused Control UI chat tests pass across composer persistence, chat state, chat send, and chat view; targeted formatting and `pnpm check:test-types` also pass; hosted `check-lint` is running on this final head. The storage-only marker is retained across internal normalization only for affected failed attachment records and is stripped from public queue snapshots.

## Real behavior evidence

The original branch was validated with a real Chrome upload of a 9.18 MB, 8-page PDF (roughly a 12 MB base64 data URL) against a live gateway. The upload completed without `RangeError`, was offloaded, and the model received extracted page content. That live run was on the pre-port head; this update ports the same stack-safe parsing behavior to today's gateway and UI paths and adds exact-path regression tests. No new live Signal/provider/device claim is being made for this merge-only port.

Generated with AI assistance; all security-sensitive parsing remains fail-closed for malformed payloads.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Terminal-control sanitization across the codebase guards untrusted text before it reaches a terminal or log, preventing ANSI escape / log-forging injection (CWE-117). The canonical range is C0 (0x00–0x1f), DEL (0x7f), **and C1 (0x80–0x9f)** — the range already used by the shared `sanitizeForLog` in `packages/terminal-core/src/ansi.ts` and by `renderTerminalBufferText` (merged in #103274). The C1 range includes the 8-bit CSI introducer **U+009B** (equivalent to `ESC [`).

Several output sinks had drifted: they covered C0/DEL but not C1, so a C1 byte (e.g. U+009B) passed through into terminal/log output. Rather than land these as isolated one-sink patches (per maintainer feedback on #103226), this is a single **deliberate, sink-wide pass**: it audits every control-character sink, closes the C1 gap in the terminal/log output sinks, and documents why the remaining sinks are already covered, out of scope, or deferred.

## Sink-wide audit

### ① Fixed here — C1 added to terminal/log output sinks (each with a focused regression test)

| Sink (function) | File | Action on control chars |
|---|---|---|
| `hasControlCharacter` (gates `buildProviderReauthCommand`) | `src/agents/failover-error.ts` | reject (suppress command) |
| `sanitizeModelWarningValue` | `src/agents/model-selection-shared.ts` | truncate at first control |
| `hasUnsafeControlChars` | `src/agents/sandbox/runtime-status.ts` | gate (agent-only fallback) |
| `escapeControlCharsVisible` | `src/agents/tool-policy-audit.ts` | escape → `\xNN` |
| `validateAttachmentName` + `describeRejectedName` | `src/agents/subagent-attachments.ts` | reject + escape diagnostic |
| `sanitizeInlineDirectiveText` | `src/agents/tools/image-generate-tool.ts` | escape → `\uNNNN` |
| `scrubDoctorErrorMessage` | `src/flows/doctor-error-message.ts` | strip |
| `sanitizeLookupPathForLog` | `src/gateway/server-methods/config.ts` | replace → `?` |
| `sanitizeForConsole` | `src/agents/console-sanitize.ts` | strip |
| `escapeControlCharsForTerminal` | `src/commands/doctor-state-integrity.ts` | escape → `\xNN` |
| `replaceLogControlCharacters` (via `formatHookErrorForLog`) | `src/hooks/fire-and-forget.ts` | replace → space |
| `formatDiagnosticValue` | `src/infra/restart-handoff.ts` | replace → space |

Each keeps its own action; only the control-code classification is aligned with `sanitizeForLog`'s range. **Why not just call `sanitizeForLog`?** It strips *all* control + ANSI *and* removes tabs/newlines, and lacks these sinks' semantics — visible escaping, `?` replacement, boundary truncation, rejection, whitespace-flattening, length caps, and optional-value handling. The right boundary is the local predicate at each sink; this PR only completes the shared range there.

### ② Already C1-complete (unchanged, referenced for coverage)

- `sanitizeForLog` — `packages/terminal-core/src/ansi.ts` (canonical range).
- `renderTerminalBufferText` — `src/gateway/terminal/buffer-text.ts` (#103274, merged).

### ③ In-scope but deferred

- `sanitizeHookConsoleValue` — `src/gateway/server/hooks.ts`. A console-warning sink that is genuinely in scope, but its only caller is inside the full gateway hook request handler; it warrants dedicated integration coverage. Deferred to a follow-up rather than shipping an untested one-liner here.

### ④ Considered and excluded (different threat model — not terminal/log output injection)

- `hasPromptUnsafeControlCharacter` — `src/agents/subagent-spawn.ts`: no-op for C1; the immediately-following ASCII allowlist already rejects it (this was #103401, closed).
- `stripDisallowedChatControlChars` — `src/gateway/chat-input-sanitize.ts`: chat-message **input** sanitization routed to channels; tab/LF/CR intentionally preserved.
- `sanitizeMediaDirectiveValue` — `src/agents/internal-events.ts`: builds prompt/runtime-context text, not terminal output.
- `sanitizeArgs` — `src/plugins/commands.ts`; `stripControlChars` — `src/cli/windows-argv.ts`: argv/plugin-arg normalization (input side).
- Input/URL/JSON-validity validators (`validateNoControlChars` in acp, `hasControlOrWhitespace` in scp-host, `normalizeProviderFinalUrl` in web-fetch, `isControlCharacter` in `packages/ai` JSON escaping) — reject/validate for other reasons; C1 is not an ANSI-injection concern there.

## Testing / Proof

All twelve fixed sinks have a focused regression using a **valid** U+009B sequence (CSI + `31m`, since U+009B is itself the complete introducer — no extra `[`). Per-file `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run <file>` results:

| Test file | Result |
|---|---|
| `agents/failover-error.test.ts` | 98 passed (incl. C1 provider-id rejection) |
| `agents/model-selection-shared.test.ts` | 2 passed (C1 boundary truncation) |
| `agents/sandbox-explain.test.ts` | 6 passed (session-label escaping + agent-only fallback) |
| `agents/subagent-attachments.test.ts` | 3 passed (C1 name rejected + escaped diagnostic) |
| `agents/tools/image-generate-tool.test.ts` | 57 passed |
| `agents/console-sanitize.test.ts` | 3 passed |
| `commands/doctor-state-integrity.test.ts` | 33 passed (+1 skipped) |
| `flows/doctor-error-message.test.ts` | 4 passed |
| `hooks/fire-and-forget.test.ts` | 6 passed (`formatHookErrorForLog`) |
| `infra/restart-handoff.test.ts` | 11 passed |
| `gateway/server-methods/config.test.ts` | new C1 test passes ✅ (see note) |

> Note on `config.test.ts`: four sibling `config.openFile` tests hard-code POSIX `/tmp/...` paths and assert the full path string. On my local **Windows** checkout the handler resolves those to `D:\tmp\...`, so they fail identically on `main` (unrelated to this change) and pass on Linux CI. The new `replaces C1 control characters in the logged failed config path` test deliberately asserts only the sanitized `cfg?.json` fragment, so it is green on both platforms.

Real code-point evidence (before → after) for `sanitizeModelWarningValue`, toggling only the one-line predicate: on current `main` a providerless model `gpt4<U+0080>EVIL` logs `Model "gpt4EVIL" ...` (residual C1 dropped, attacker suffix retained); with this change it logs `Model "gpt4" ...` (truncated at the C1 boundary).

## Relationship to the open C1 PRs

This supersedes the seven isolated sink PRs (#103379 #103380 #103381 #103382 #103383 #103402 #103405) and re-lands the `sanitizeForConsole` fix from the closed #103226 cleanly (valid U+009B test, no proof-only scripts). Those PRs will be closed in favor of this consolidated review.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
